result: {"episodeSummary": "In a guest-free episode of FS Jam, the hosts unpack the little-documented craft of building third-party scripts and widgets, drawing on lessons from creating Everfund's donation widget. They cover choosing a bundler and module format, why UMD remains necessary alongside CommonJS and ESM, and tooling failures that forced a Rollup workaround, plus hosting choices between npm CDNs and private buckets, browser support trade-offs, and a stubborn WordPress incompatibility solved by self-hosting the script. They compare iframe-based widgets with injecting content into the DOM, weighing CORS, CSS encapsulation, and customization trade-offs, along with the size gap between vanilla JS and React SDKs and a shift toward a headless donation API. The conversation then turns to the podcast itself: more no-guest deep dives, documentation practices like the Divio system and tools such as ReadMe and Docusaurus, attending Remix Conf, and introducing sponsorships. Anthony emphasizes educating first as a developer advocate and carefully vetting guests and sponsors, citing one product he regrets promoting. They close with favorite recent episodes and a goal of keeping FS Jam sustainable while serving as a lasting record for future developers."}
